title: Beyond Accuracy: Handling Extreme Class Imbalance in Real-World Marketing Conversion Prediction
content: In real-world marketing applications, predictive modeling tasks often encounter severe class imbalance, where positive conversion events constitute only a small fraction of the overall observations. Under such conditions, traditional accuracy metrics can be highly misleading, masking poor performance on the cases that matter most to decision-makers. This study presents a comparative evaluation of modeling strategies for imbalanced marketing data, using a publicly available bank marketing dataset as a case study. The analysis examines baseline classifiers, methods of resampling (such as SMOTE), cost-sensitive learning, and ensemble-based models, with a primary focus on precision–recall trade-offs, the PR-AUC metric, and calibrated decision thresholds. The results indicate that models optimized for accuracy systematically perform poorly in identifying rare conversion events. In contrast, recall-sensitive and cost-oriented strategies—especially when combined with proper threshold tuning—lead to significantly improved business-relevant outcomes. This study demonstrates how existing machine learning techniques can be strategically configured, evaluated, and calibrated to deliver meaningful and actionable value in real-world marketing conversion prediction tasks characterized by extreme class imbalance.
